sources.name: Brysbaert (2019), How many words do we read per minute? A review and meta-analysis of reading rate, Journal of Memory and Language 109:104047
sources.measures: Mean silent reading rate of healthy adult native speakers aged 17-60 reading normal text for comprehension, pooled across 190 published studies (1901-2019, mostly English, predominantly university students). Unweighted random-effects mean of study-level means. Words counted as published by each study (no character normalisation).
sources.notes: 238 wpm is the unweighted mean across studies (95% CI 230-246); 235 is the MEDIAN OF STUDY MEANS, not a person-level median. SD 51.2 is the between-study SD of study means, not the between-person SD. Weighted subset (87 studies, 10,201 participants, with reported SDs): mean 247.5 wpm, SD 47.4. Mean for fiction 260 wpm, non-fiction 238 wpm. Paper states 'most adults fall in the range of 175-300 wpm' for non-fiction and '200-320 wpm' for fiction; this is a descriptive range, not a stated percentile. Largest single study inside the meta-analysis: Taylor (1965), 12,143 readers grades 1 to college, college students 280 wpm. No percentile table of individual readers is published. Full text read from the author-archived PDF (gwern.net/doc/psychology/linguistics/2019-brysbaert.pdf); data at https://osf.io/3wfas/.

definition: Mean silent reading rate of healthy adult native speakers aged 17-60 reading normal text for comprehension, pooled across 190 published studies (1901-2019, mostly English, predominantly university students). Unweighted random-effects mean of study-level means. Words counted as published by each study (no character normalisation).
caveat: No credible source publishes a 99th percentile (or any percentile) of adult silent reading speed; the best sources give only means, between-study SDs, and descriptive ranges, so a top-1% value cannot be reported without deriving it. Measurement is not standardised: Brysbaert's pooled figure mixes short one-minute tests and hour-long texts, counts 'words' as each study did (English word ~4.6-5.1 letters), and covers native-speaking adults 17-60 who are mostly university students (WEIRD samples), not all adults worldwide. The only person-level SD (260 ± 87 wpm) comes from 48 self-selected highly educated book readers. Bookmate data are Russian-language and truncated above 300 wpm. Comprehension is only loosely controlled; speed without comprehension (skimming, RSVP) can reach 790-1652 wpm in lab tests (Rubin & Turano 1992, n=9) but is a different construct. Rayner et al. 2016 argue rates above roughly 500-750 wpm are not compatible with normal comprehension.

new_metric.label: Silent reading speed
new_metric.definition: Words per minute read silently, with comprehension, when reading ordinary continuous text at one's normal pace.
